1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module nineteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. The time budget. The routine for every task. Using the documentation well. Domain checklists. Common traps. The final week.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All five domains. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: the commands in this module were used in the executed labs of Modules zero to sixteen.

1.title: The time budget
1.text: The time budget. The figure shows this: The time budget. Exam tip: Plan about six to eight minutes per task, easy tasks first, and keep about ten minutes to verify.

1.title: The time budget, continued
1.text: The time budget. The exam is two hours for fifteen to twenty tasks. That is an average of six to eight minutes per task, with the passing score at sixty-six percent. Points differ per task (the exact points per task are not published on the pages used for this course), so.

1.title: The time budget, continued
1.text: The time budget. Spend the first two minutes skimming the whole list if the interface allows; otherwise start in order. find the quick wins early. Do easy tasks first, flag hard ones. one fifteen-minute task can cost two easy ones. If you are stuck after about six minutes, flag it and move on. partial progress on many tasks beats perfection on few. Keep ten minutes at the end to re-verify. a typo in a namespace costs a full task. Do not leave a task half-broken (a half-edited manifest). the checker sees the final state.

1.title: The time budget, continued
1.text: The time budget. Where the points are (by domain weight): Environment, Configuration and Security twenty-five percent, then Design and Build, Deployment and Services and Networking at twenty percent each, and Observability and Maintenance fifteen percent. The C K A D has no node or cluster administration: almost every task is a kube control task in a namespace, and many are quick.

1.title: The routine for every task
1.text: The routine for every task. Read the whole task, including the last line (names, namespaces, "do not change..."). Run the context line ( kube control config use context... ). Check with kube control config current context. Note exact names, namespaces, ports, labels, image tags, file paths. Copy them from the task text, never retype from memory. Do it with the fastest tool (imperative command, the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml, kube control explain, one docs page). Verify with a different command from the one that created it (create with kube control create, verify with kube control get dash o wide, describe, logs or a test Pod). Move on. Exam tip: Verify each task with a second command before you move on.

1.title: Using the documentation well
1.text: Using the documentation well. You may use Kubernetes dot I O or docs and blog, helm dot S H or docs, the Quick Reference links in the exam, and distribution documents under slash usr slash share. You may use the Kubernetes dot I O search; you must not open results from outside the allowed sites. Learn where things are before the exam: Concepts for explanations, Tasks for step-by-step yamel (Pods and containers, probes, Config Maps, Secrets, security context, volumes and P V (Persistent Volume) slash P V C (Persistent Volume Claim), Jobs, Ingress), Reference for the kube control cheat sheet. Prefer kube control explain for field names (faster than the browser). Copy examples, then change names; do not retype a long yamel. Browser tabs and the terminal share the screen; practice with only the allowed pages.

1.title: Domain checklists
1.text: Domain checklists. Environment, Configuration and Security (twenty-five percent): Config Map and Secret ( create, env or env From, volumes, sub Path ), requests and limits ( set resources ), Resource Quota and Limit Range ( describe quota ), Service Account ( service Account Name, automount Service Account Token ), R back ( create role slash rolebinding, auth can i ), security Context (Pod and container level, capabilities), Pod Security labels, C R Ds ( explain, api resources ). Application Design and Build (twenty percent): image ( build dash t, save, tags), command and args, image Pull Policy, Job and Cron Job ( completions, parallelism, the from flag set to cronjob or ), Daemon Set or Stateful Set yamel, init containers, sidecars, empty dir, P V or P V C or Storage Class.

1.title: Domain checklists, continued
1.text: Domain checklists. Application Deployment (twenty percent): rolling update ( set image, rollout status slash history slash undo slash pause slash resume, max Surge or max Unavailable ), blue or green (Service selector), canary (replica ratio), Helm ( repo add, install the set flag slash dash f, upgrade, rollback, template, get values ), Kustomize ( apply dash k, overlay fields). Services and Networking (twenty percent): Services ( expose, types, port or target Port, endpoints), D N S names, Ingress (class, host and path, path Type, T L S Secret), Network Policy (and versus or, D N S for egress, deny-all). Observability and Maintenance (fifteen percent): probes (liveness, readiness, startup; H T T P get, exec, T C P socket ), A P I versions ( api resources ), get, describe, logs the previous flag dash c, top, exec, debug, events.

1.title: Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab)
1.text: Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab). Wrong cluster context. run and verify the context line. Wrong namespace (object created in default ). dash n on every command, or set the context namespace; verify with get dash A then pipe to grep name. Resource created but misspelled name. copy names from the task. Pod fields are immutable. delete and recreate ( the force flag the grace period flag zero ). Added a container to a running Pod. recreate the Pod, or edit the Deployment. Env var from a Config Map not updated. restart the Pods ( rollout restart ). A claim without storage Class Name and a P V with manual. give both the same class. Exam tip: Check the first three traps on every task: the wrong context, the wrong namespace and a misspelled name; copy names from the task.

1.title: Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab), continued
1.text: Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab). role Ref immutable. delete and recreate the binding. Network Policy blocks D N S. allow U D P and T C P fifty-three in egress. Selector typo equals no endpoints. get endpoints, the show labels flag. latest tag and a local image. image Pull Policy If Not Present or a real tag. Probe on the wrong path or port. describe pod, test with exec... W get. Left an answer unverified. verify every task. Rebooted base or used the Insert key. not allowed.

1.title: The final week
1.text: The final week. Redo the break-and-fix labs until you can do each in under six minutes: crash loop back off, image pull back off, create container config error, Pending, probes, Service with no endpoints, Ingress four oh four. Run the two timed mixed sets (Modules seventeen and eighteen) under exam conditions: two hours, only the allowed documentation. Use the killer dot S H simulator that comes with the exam registration (two attempts of thirty-six hours each, seventeen questions per session): it is the closest to the real environment. Practice the speed kit (Module zero) until k, do and kube control explain are automatic. Re-read the Quick Reference Cards of every module.

1.title: The final week, continued
1.text: The final week. Check the current curriculum version and the exam page before booking: the exam moves to a new Kubernetes version a few weeks after each release; rules, fees and allowed resources can change.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How much time per task do you have on average? Answer: About six to eight minutes (two hours for fifteen to twenty tasks). Question two. What should you do after about six minutes on a stuck task? Answer: Flag it and move on; return at the end. Question three. What is the first thing you do in each task? Answer: Run the context line and note exact names and namespaces.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name two fast ways to avoid hand-writing yamel. Answer: the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml and copying examples from the documentation. Question five. Which tool beats the browser for field names? Answer: kube control explain. Question six. What is the passing score? Answer: sixty-six percent.

1.title: Recall Check 3
1.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. Which domain carries the highest weight? Answer: Application Environment, Configuration and Security, twenty-five percent. Question eight. Which simulator is included with the exam registration? Answer: killer dot S H (two attempts of thirty-six hours each).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Time: two hours, fifteen to twenty tasks, about six to eight minutes each, sixty-six percent to pass. Order: easy first, flag hard, ten minutes to verify. Every task: context line, exact names, verify with a second command. Docs: Kubernetes dot I O and helm dot S H only. Weights: Env twenty-five, Design twenty, Deployment twenty, Networking twenty, Observability fifteen. Practice: break-and-fix labs, timed sets, killer dot S H. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
